stops.name: The finished Temple, seven years, the throne of the lions
stops.campa: In seven years the house is finished in all its parts: the holy place overlaid with pure gold, the two cherubim of olive wood, wings touching wall to wall over the oracle, the pillars Jachin and Boaz, the molten sea on twelve oxen, the lampstands and the pomegranates. Solomon makes a great throne of ivory overlaid with the best gold, six steps, twelve lions standing on either side; there was not the like made in any kingdom. In the aggadah the lions and eagles are wrought with cunning: they stretch their paws to bear the king up step by step, and roar against any liar who dares to mount.
stops.quote: There was not the like made in any kingdom.

stops.name: The plain of Jordan at Zarethan, Hiram casts the pillars and the sea
stops.campa: Hiram of Tyre, the widow's son of Naphtali, filled with wisdom to work all works in brass, comes to King Solomon and casts the great bronze in the clay ground of the Jordan, between Succoth and Zarethan. He casts the two pillars, Jachin on the right hand, Boaz on the left, each eighteen cubits high, crowned with lily-work and pomegranates and chapiters of net. He casts the molten sea, ten cubits from brim to brim, resting upon twelve oxen that look to the four winds, holding two thousand baths of water for the priests' washing. The bronze is beyond weight or reckoning; the vessels of the house shine.
stops.quote: In the plain of Jordan did the king cast them, in the clay ground between Succoth and Zarthan.

stops.name: The dedication, the cloud of glory fills the house
stops.campa: At the feast in the seventh month the priests bring up the Ark of the covenant of the Lord into the oracle, under the wings of the cherubim, into the most holy place; within it only the two tables of stone that Moses put there at Horeb. As the priests come out of the holy place, the cloud fills the house of the Lord, so that they cannot stand to minister: for the glory of the Lord has filled the house. Then Solomon spreads his hands to heaven and prays: the God whom the heaven of heavens cannot contain has come to dwell in the house he has built.
stops.quote: The cloud filled the house of the LORD, so that the priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud: for the glory of the LORD had filled the house of the LORD.

stops.name: Jerusalem, the Lord appears the second time, the warning
stops.campa: When Solomon has finished the house of the Lord and the king's house and all his desire, the Lord appears to him the second time, as He had appeared at Gibeon. He tells the king: I have heard your prayer; I have hallowed this house to put my name there for ever. But the promise is bound with a warning: if you or your children turn from me and serve other gods, then I will cut off Israel from the land, and this house which is high shall be an astonishment, and every one that passes by shall hiss. The blessing carries within it the word of ruin.
stops.quote: But if ye shall at all turn from following me, ye or your children... then will I cut off Israel out of the land which I have given them.

stops.name: Jerusalem, the thousand and five songs, the speech of trees
stops.campa: God gives Solomon wisdom and understanding exceeding much, and largeness of heart even as the sand upon the sea shore. He is wiser than all men, than Ethan and Heman and the sons of Mahol; his fame is in all the nations round about. He speaks three thousand proverbs, and his songs are a thousand and five. He speaks of trees, from the cedar of Lebanon to the hyssop that springs out of the wall; he speaks of beasts and of fowl and of creeping things and of fishes. Kings of the earth send to hear the wisdom that God has put into his heart.
stops.quote: And his songs were a thousand and five. And he spake of trees, from the cedar tree that is in Lebanon even unto the hyssop that springeth out of the wall.

stops.name: The Valley of the Ants, Sulayman and the speech of the creatures
stops.campa: Sulayman is taught the speech of the birds; he inherits from Dawud and is given of all things. His hosts are gathered, jinn and men and birds, and set in ranks, and he marches. When they come upon the Valley of the Ants, one ant cries out: 'O ants, enter your dwellings, lest Sulayman and his hosts crush you while they perceive not!' And Sulayman smiles, laughing at her speech, and prays that he may be thankful for the favour God has bestowed on him and on his parents, and do the righteousness that pleases Him. The whole earth is legible to the king whom God has taught.
stops.quote: So he smiled, amused at her speech, and said: My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favour which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents.

stops.name: Jerusalem, the twelve officers and the peace of Judah and Israel
stops.campa: Solomon has twelve officers over all Israel, each providing victuals for the king and his household one month in the year: fine flour and meal, fat oxen and pastured oxen, sheep, harts, roebucks, fallow-deer, and fatted fowl. He reigns over all kingdoms from the River unto the border of Egypt, and they bring presents and serve him all his days. Judah and Israel dwell safely, every man under his vine and under his fig tree, from Dan even to Beersheba, all the days of Solomon. He has forty thousand stalls of horses for his chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen. There is peace on all sides round about him.
stops.quote: And Judah and Israel dwelt safely, every man under his vine and under his fig tree, from Dan even to Beersheba, all the days of Solomon.

stops.name: The muster of the birds, the hoopoe's absence
stops.campa: Sulayman inspects the birds and finds a gap in the ranks: 'Why do I not see the hoopoe? Or is he among the absent? I will surely punish him severely, or slaughter him, unless he brings me a clear authority.' The hoopoe is not long in coming, and says: I have encompassed what you have not, and I bring you from Sheba certain news. There is a woman ruling them, given of all things, and a mighty throne; but I found her and her people prostrating to the sun instead of God, their deeds made fair by Satan. The king sends her a letter by the bird's own wing.
stops.quote: But the hoopoe stayed not long: he (came up and) said: I have compassed (territory) which thou hast not compassed, and I have come to thee from Saba with tidings true.

stops.name: The wind at his command, the throne of Bilqis brought in a blink
stops.campa: To Sulayman God subjects the wind: its morning course a month's journey, its evening course a month's journey; and He makes a fount of molten brass to flow for him; and of the jinn are those who work before him by his Lord's leave, building sanctuaries and statues and basins like reservoirs, and diving in the sea for pearls. When the queen's throne is to be fetched, one with knowledge of the Book says, 'I will bring it to thee before thy gaze returns to thee', and it stands before Sulayman in the twinkling of an eye. He says, this is of the bounty of my Lord.
stops.quote: And to Solomon (We made) the Wind (obedient): Its early morning (stride) was a month's (journey), and its evening (stride) was a month's (journey).

stops.name: Marib, the queen of Sheba hears the fame of Solomon
stops.campa: Far to the south, in the land of spices where the incense-trees weep their gum, the queen of Sheba hears the fame of Solomon concerning the name of the Lord. In the Kebra Nagast her name is Makeda, and the merchant Tamrin tells her of a king whose wisdom the world cannot measure. She resolves to go up and prove him with hard questions. She sets out with a very great train, camels bearing spices and gold in abundance and precious stones, the long caravan winding north out of Arabia toward Jerusalem, to see whether the half of what is told can be true.
stops.quote: And when the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon concerning the name of the LORD, she came to prove him with hard questions.

stops.name: Jerusalem, the hard questions and the failing spirit
stops.campa: The queen comes to Jerusalem and communes with Solomon of all that is in her heart, and there is nothing hid from the king that he does not tell her. She sees all his wisdom, the house he has built, the meat of his table, the sitting of his servants, the ascent by which he goes up unto the house of the Lord, and there is no more spirit in her. It was a true report I heard, she says, howbeit I believed not, until mine eyes had seen; and the half was not told me. In the Kebra Nagast she forsakes the sun and bears Menelik.
stops.quote: It was a true report that I heard in mine own land of thy acts and of thy wisdom. Howbeit I believed not the words, until I came, and mine eyes had seen it: and, behold, the half was not told me.

stops.name: The court of the crystal floor, the queen of Sheba submits (Bilqis)
stops.campa: In the Quranic telling, the hoopoe carries Sulayman's letter to Bilqis, sealed 'In the name of Allah, be not arrogant, but come to me in submission.' She sends gifts to test him; he refuses them and threatens hosts she cannot withstand. One with knowledge of the Book fetches her throne in the blink of an eye, disguised, and she half-knows it. Then she is bidden enter the pavilion, its floor a smooth court of glass over flowing water; she thinks it a pool and bares her legs. Sulayman tells her: it is a palace paved with crystal. And she submits with Sulayman to the Lord of the Worlds.
stops.quote: She said: O my Lord! I have indeed wronged my soul: I do (now) submit (in Islam), with Solomon, to the Lord of the Worlds.
